visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 more accurately visualizes the actual pendulum setup, small-angle geometry, formula components, and gravity/length relationships, whereas Lesson 2 is mostly generic static slides with little diagrammatic representation of the physical system and some misleading/irrelevant visual framing despite having mostly correct equations.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons have absent gate specs and absent plan JSON, so neither shows any functioning checkpoints or input-rendering gates.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 is severely garbled and unnatural throughout, but Lesson 1 has no narration transcript at all to assess and is treated as absent, making Lesson 2 marginally preferable despite its major narration defects.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 at least provides a narration transcript, but neither lesson supplies visual cue timing needed to verify synchronization, while Lesson 1 is entirely absent and therefore demonstrates even less sync evidence.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is highly garbled and contains a confusing erroneous mention of 0.45 m, but it at least uses the correct pendulum-period relationship implicitly and reaches the correct result of pi seconds, whereas Lesson 1 has no available teaching content to verify or learn from at all.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has consistently large, legible text and a cohesive slide design, whereas Lesson 1 is sparse with tiny text, weak contrast/faint formula elements, off-center compositions, and some awkward label overlap, though Lesson 2 is held back by persistent cursor/footer/subtitle UI artifacts.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the overall winner by a clear confidence-weighted majority. Lesson 1 wins visual accuracy strongly, with better pendulum diagrams and geometry, while interactivity is a full-confidence tie because neither lesson provides functioning gates or plan JSON. However, Lesson 2 is preferred on narration, synchronization evidence, concept accuracy, and polish. These wins are not uniformly strong—narration and sync are only marginal because Lesson 2 is garbled and lacks timing evidence—but Lesson 1 is often treated as absent or insufficient in those areas. Lesson 2 also better conveys the correct pendulum-period result and has more polished, legible slide design despite artifacts. Overall, the accumulated weighted support favors Lesson 2.
